content: 1. Tubular Reabsorption and pH Effects: Increased pH can lead to enhanced passive renal tubular reabsorption. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Salicylate levels tend to increase at moderate doses but decrease at higher doses due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. 2. Calcium Carbonate and Acalabrutinib: Calcium carbonate reduces the levels of acalabrutinib by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the solubility of acalabrutinib. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. It is recommended to separate the administration of antacids and acalabrutinib by at least 2 hours. 3. Calcium Carbonate and Acebutolol: Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of acebutolol through an unspecified mechanism and reduces its levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 4. Calcium Carbonate and Alendronate: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of alendronate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 30 minutes. 5. Calcium Carbonate and Allopurinol: Calcium carbonate reduces the levels of allopurinol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 6. Calcium Carbonate and Amantadine: Calcium carbonate increases the levels or effects of amantadine due to changes in urine pH toward alkalinity, which may lead to the accumulation of amantadine and an increased risk of adverse reactions. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Monitor for potential adverse effects of amantadine. 7. Calcium Carbonate and Amikacin: Amikacin decreases the levels of calcium carbonate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 8. Calcium Carbonate and Amiloride: Amiloride decreases the levels of calcium carbonate by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 9. Calcium Carbonate and Amlodipine: Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of amlodipine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Calcium Carbonate and Amphetamine: Calcium carbonate increases the levels or effects of amphetamine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Calcium Carbonate and Aspirin: Calcium carbonate interacts with aspirin through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses but decrease at higher doses due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 12. Calcium Carbonate and Atazanavir: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH, which reduces the solubility of atazanavir. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Administer atazanavir 2 hours before or 1 hour after calcium carbonate. 13. Calcium Carbonate and Atenolol: Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of atenolol through an unspecified mechanism and decreases its levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 14. Calcium Carbonate and Azithromycin: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of azithromycin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 15. Calcium Carbonate and Baloxavir Marboxil: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of baloxavir marboxil by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Baloxavir may bind to polyvalent cations, leading to decreased absorption. Studies in monkeys have shown significantly reduced plasma levels when co-administered with calcium, aluminum, or iron. Human studies have not been conducted. 16. Calcium Carbonate and Balsalazide: Calcium carbonate interacts with balsalazide through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses but decrease at higher doses due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 17. Calcium Carbonate and Benazepril: Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of benazepril through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Calcium Carbonate and Bendroflumethiazide: Bendroflumethiazide increases the levels of calcium carbonate by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction may increase the risk of alkalosis and hypercalcemia. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 19. Calcium Carbonate and Benzphetamine: Calcium carbonate increases the levels or effects of benzphetamine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Calcium Carbonate and Betaxolol: Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of betaxolol through an unspecified mechanism and decreases its levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours.
